why: The left-hand side of the equation this is the right-hand side of. It stops exactly where this target starts, which is the point: `C_N` cites the paper, so 'the rest of my own sentence' is expressible as a citation and `cn_errors` can still prove the two do not overlap.
And what this $D$ is. The paper introduces it as a map $\R^J\to\R^I$; the Lean side is a `Matrix I J ℝ`. Two levels up that identification is invisible — here it is the edge.

What the sum has to satisfy, which is the only reason this is a sum at all: the second summand is supported at a single position of $T$, so adding it keeps the support inside $T$. The claim is the tail of the sentence this formula sits in, not part of the formula.
And the definition that makes 'still supported on $T$' a checkable statement about the sum rather than a word about it. It is eight sentences back, in the paragraph before the lemma.
The only place $\tau$ is ever quantified, and the only place its nonzeroness is stated. This formula uses the symbol as if it were already in scope; the binder is in the clause before.

The only introduction $s$ and $j$ ever get. $e_s$ and $e_j^{\mathsf T}$ are not defined anywhere in the paper — the notation is assumed — so the edge from `Matrix.single s j 1` to $e_s e_j^{\mathsf T}$ is judged against a convention rather than a definition. That is a fact about the paper worth recording, and a citation with a reason is where it can be recorded.
